explanation: Count each character, then count how many frequencies are odd. Mirrored positions use pairs, so only an optional middle position can consume an unpaired character.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time. Each character updates one expected-constant-time hash entry.
spaceComplexity: O(u) auxiliary space for u distinct characters. At most u distinct characters have parity/count state.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/is_string_permutable_to_palindrome.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: A palindrome requires all characters outside its center to occur in pairs, so at most one count can be odd. Conversely, pair half of each frequency symmetrically and put the one remaining odd character in the center. The Counter parity test is therefore necessary and sufficient.
walkthrough: For bbcaac, Counter gives b:2,c:2,a:2. The sum of count mod 2 is zero, so return true; abccba is one valid permutation.
edgeCases: An empty string passes with no odd counts.
Two or more odd-frequency characters fail.
